brief: Nomura's McElligott says the unwind of 2026's popular momentum/high-Sharpe thematic positioning has been acute over the past month-plus, confirmed by prime-broker data showing net and gross exposure falling, with some trades nearing full round-trip levels. He raises whether long/short and market-neutral hedge funds, focused on protecting full-year performance and capital ahead of the Q4/year-end turn, can or want to re-risk into the resulting opportunity set. This unwind has driven the average S&P 500 stock to move 13.2% (absolute) over the past month versus just 1.1% at the index level, a 12.1-point dispersion spread at the 100th percentile of a 30-year lookback, with top/bottom-decile dispersion at the 99th percentile. He argues this extreme historically precedes a rare bearish 'stocks down, vol down' signal: SPX median/mean returns of -3.8% at 3 months and -13.4%/-2.0% at 12 months, alongside a VIX collapse across the forward period, as the dispersion shock marks a local vol high before both vol and the index fade.
